name: Mintsoft
tagline: Cloud warehouse management and order fulfilment software aimed at 3PLs and e-commerce fulfilment operations.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The screens are boring: stock locations, inbound goods, pick lists, despatch, invoices. An agent can reproduce those in a weekend and it will look fine in a demo. What it cannot reproduce is the long tail of courier and marketplace connections, the label formats each carrier insists on, the tracking webhooks, and the per-client billing rules a 3PL runs its revenue on. Multi-client warehousing also drags in audit trails, stock accuracy disputes, and the kind of edge cases that only show up at volume. If you run a real warehouse, a DIY version is a liability, not a saving.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-warehouse inventory and order app: import orders by CSV, generate pick lists, record picks and despatches, and keep an auditable stock ledger.
requirements: Node 20 and a local machine or small VPS
A barcode scanner that behaves as a keyboard, optional
Carrier accounts and manual label creation, because the build does not integrate couriers
whatYouLose: Courier integrations, rate shopping, and compliant label generation
Marketplace and cart connectors with order and stock sync both ways
Per-client 3PL billing: storage, pick fees, surcharges, invoicing
Mobile scanning apps, multi-warehouse and multi-user permissions
Someone to call when stock numbers and reality disagree
moatNotes: The product is really a hub of carrier and channel connectors wearing a WMS as a coat.
whyPeopleStillPay: A 3PL does not buy screens, it buys the fact that an order from a marketplace lands in the right client's queue, gets a label the carrier will actually accept, pushes tracking back to the channel, and ends up on the right monthly invoice. Every one of those links is somebody else's API with its own quirks and its own breakage schedule, and keeping them alive is a full time job. Once your clients' orders flow through a system, ripping it out mid-peak is unthinkable, so the switching cost does the rest of the selling.
notes: The stock ledger is a weekend; the connector fleet is not. The moat is hundreds of carrier and channel integrations plus the 3PL billing rules nobody wants to re-derive.
prompt:
Build a local-first warehouse inventory and order fulfilment app for a single small warehouse. No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 14 App Router with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/wms.db
- Drizzle ORM for schema and migrations
- Tailwind CSS, plain server actions, no component library
- Vitest for a few unit tests on stock math

Data model:
- products: sku, name, barcode, unit, reorder_point
- locations: code, zone, type (bulk or pick)
- stock_ledger: append-only rows with product_id, location_id, qty_delta, reason (receipt, pick, adjust, return), ref, created_at
- orders and order_lines: external_ref, customer name, address fields, status (new, picking, picked, despatched, cancelled)
- current stock is always derived from the ledger, never stored as a mutable number

Features in scope:
- CSV import for products and for orders, with a dry-run preview and row-level error reporting
- Goods-in screen: scan or type a barcode, pick a location, record a receipt
- Allocation: assign stock to order lines from pick locations, oldest order first, flag shortages
- Pick list: printable HTML per wave, sorted by zone then location code, with checkboxes
- Picking confirmation by barcode scan, partial picks allowed, writes ledger rows
- Despatch: mark order despatched, store a manually entered tracking number and carrier string
- Stock adjustments with a mandatory reason note
- Reports: stock on hand by product and location, movements for a date range, below-reorder-point list, all exportable to CSV

Explicitly out of scope, do not stub fake versions:
- Carrier APIs, rate shopping, label generation
- Marketplace or shopping cart integrations
- Multi-client 3PL billing and invoicing
- Mobile native app, multi-warehouse, user roles

Requirements:
- Barcode input fields must work with a keyboard-wedge scanner: autofocus, submit on Enter, no mouse needed
- All mutations go through server actions inside a transaction; ledger rows are never updated or deleted
- Seed script with 40 products, 20 locations, 15 orders
- .env.example for DB_PATH only, no secrets needed otherwise
- README with setup, import CSV column formats, and a blunt note that this is not a substitute for a real WMS in a multi-client operation
